semantic_rules.rule: For volume, quieter maps to down, louder to up, silence to mute. “Change the volume” gives no direction.
For alarms, asking which are already set is alarm_query. Asking to create one is alarm_set. Asking to cancel one is alarm_remove.
Distinguish changing your schedule, checking existing entries and seeking suggestions for things to do.
For lights, distinguish power, brightness direction and colour by the change requested.
Use the controlled object: a plug, a cleaner and a coffee maker can all be switched on.
A named person can be a contact lookup, a contact being saved, a sender filter or a recipient; use the requested operation.
Use the requested medium; identifying what is playing and changing a playback setting differ from requesting content.
Distinguish approval from disapproval of the music; mention alone establishes neither.
Distinguish adding, removing and reading list contents even when the same item is named.
A request to convert between time frames differs from asking the time at one location.
Distinguish an exchange rate between currencies from a financial instrument’s price.
Reading social content differs from publishing it; the same platform can be named in both.
Distinguish placing a food order from asking about availability or an existing delivery.
Distinguish directions, obtaining a ticket, traffic conditions and requesting a ride.
Distinguish greeting the assistant from asking it to tell a joke.
Use what is being recommended: a place or a movie; a city may occur in either request.
Distinguish asking for a meaning, a calculation and a factual answer by the operation requested.
